summary: Replace the baseline with a multi-start SLSQP optimiser over (x, y, r), using analytic Jacobians. Starts are random or perturbations of the best solution so far, run within a time budget, and the final radii are made strictly feasible.

Raise the time budget to 230s and replace the perturbation step with more varied basin-hopping moves on the best solution: relocating small circles, swapping two circles, and jittering all centres. Random restarts are kept only for the first part of the run.

Add a final high-precision SLSQP polish (tighter ftol, more iterations) starting from the best solution found. It is kept only if it gives a larger feasible sum of radii, so it can squeeze out the last digits without risking the current result.

After the search loop, I re-solve the radii for the best centres as an exact LP (HiGHS), which gives the optimal radii for those fixed centres. The result is shrunk by a tiny margin and kept only if it is feasible and has a larger sum than the current best.
